TX.rateName: Residential Delivery Service (Wires Only - Deregulated Market)
TX.unsupportedReason: Texas ERCOT is a deregulated retail electricity market. Oncor operates solely as a transmission and distribution utility (TDSP wires company). Commodity electricity is purchased independently from competitive Retail Electric Providers (REPs). Static Time-of-Use rate schedules are not indexed in OpenEI URDB for competitive retail plans; default EIA state residential benchmark ($0.148/kWh) is applied.
TX.description: Oncor distribution delivery tariff in ERCOT deregulated market. Commodity power supply provided by third-party competitive REPs.

chargerInstallation.source: NREL / DOE EVSE Benchmarks & Utility Rebate Catalog

standard.description: Dedicated 240V 50A circuit within 25 feet of existing breaker panel with adequate spare capacity

complex.description: Extended conduit run (> 50 feet), drywall patching, or subpanel addition for detached garage

panel_upgrade.description: Main electric service panel upgrade from 100A to 200A to accommodate dedicated EV continuous load

federalSection30cRules.notes: Section 30C credit terminated on June 30, 2026 for refueling property placed in service after that date. Current default applied credit remains strictly $0.00.

utilityRebates.eligibilityCriteria: Active PG&E residential electric customers; purchase and installation of pre-approved Level 2 EVSE; limited to 1 rebate per household; covers up to 50% of equipment price (benchmarked up to $350); applications close November 11, 2026

utilityRebates.programName: PG&E Residential Charging Solutions (Rebate Plus - Income Qualified)
utilityRebates.eligibilityCriteria: Income-qualified residential customers enrolled in CARE/FERA or household income ≤ 80% Area Median Income (AMI); covers up to $2,000 for charger and installation, or up to $5,000 if electrical panel upgrade is required
Program officially closed effective June 30, 2026; no new applications accepted

utilityRebates.programName: FPL EVolution Home Charger Installation (Subscription Model)
utilityRebates.eligibilityCriteria: Turnkey monthly subscription model ($38/month covers Level 2 charger hardware, dedicated 240V installation, and ongoing maintenance; not an upfront cash rebate paid to consumer)
Eversource CT residential electric customers installing an eligible Level 2 networked charger and enrolling in managed charging demand response

utilityRebates.programName: DTE Charging Forward Residential EV Rebate
utilityRebates.eligibilityCriteria: DTE residential electric customers who install an approved smart Level 2 charger and enroll in a Time-of-Day rate (Rate D1.9)

utilityRebates.programName: Duke Energy Residential Charger Prep Credit
utilityRebates.eligibilityCriteria: Duke Energy Carolinas residential customers completing qualified 240V dedicated circuit installation by a licensed electrical contractor

national_benchmark.notes: National weighted average across Electrify America, EVgo, and Tesla non-member peak rates

electrify_america.notes: Standard Guest tier without Pass+ subscription ($7.00/mo reduces rate to ~$0.36/kWh)

tesla_supercharger.notes: Tesla owner off-peak baseline ~$0.32/kWh; peak/non-Tesla driver baseline ~$0.44/kWh

evgo.notes: Includes standard session fee for guest users in states permitting per-kWh pricing
